Firmware / Embedded Systems Engineering

Full-time

**Industry:**
Aviation & Aerospace

**About Company**

A venture-backed, seed-stage startup founded in 2023. The company is modernizing the spacecraft component supply chain for low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellite applications.

It specializes in Attitude Determination and Control System (ADCS) components — reaction wheels, star trackers, and torque rods. Headquartered in the US with operations in Bengaluru, India, the company serves satellite manufacturers and LEO constellation developers worldwide.

The team brings deep experience from high-volume space missions and is driven by a commitment to quality, affordability, and speed. The company has raised $2.2M in funding and is building critical infrastructure for the commercial space ecosystem.

**Position Overview**

This role is built for a hands-on firmware engineer who has explored embedded systems through academic projects or space club work and is ready to apply that curiosity in a real-world spacecraft hardware environment. The engineer will work on firmware for ADCS components — reaction wheels, star trackers, and torque rods — contributing to the full development cycle from bring-up to validation. **Role & Responsibilities**

* Develop and maintain firmware for ADCS hardware components including reaction wheels, star trackers, and torque rods

* Write and debug low-level embedded code for microcontrollers used in space-grade hardware
* Support hardware-software integration testing and document firmware behavior against hardware specifications

* Exposure to communication protocols such as I2C, SPI, UART, or CAN
* Active participation in a college space club, satellite team, or aerospace project (e.g., CanSat, CubeSat, rocketry, or ADCS subsystem work)

**Nice to Have**

* Project experience specifically on ADCS subsystems — attitude sensing, reaction wheels, or control algorithms

* Exposure to hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing or spacecraft simulation environments
* Experience with version control tools such as Git in a team project setting
* Prior internship or project collaboration with a space startup, ISRO student program, or aerospace research lab

* Direct ownership of firmware modules on real spacecraft hardware from day one
* Mentorship from engineers with experience across multiple space missions
* Onsite role in Bengaluru embedded within a globally connected US-India team
* Ground-floor opportunity at a seed-stage startup shaping the commercial space supply chain

# Junior IoT, AI Vision & Hardware Developer

### Entry-Level | AI Xccelerate (AIX)

\*\*Location:\*\* [Add location / on-site or hybrid]

\*\*Employment type:\*\* [Full-time / Internship / Contract]

\*\*Experience:\*\* Beginner / Entry-level; personal, college, and hobby projects welcome

## About AI Xccelerate

AI Xccelerate is an enterprise AI execution and implementation company building its own agentic framework, AI Workers, and AI Agents. We build purpose-built solutions that connect AI, software, and physical devices to solve real business problems.

We’re looking for a curious, hands-on beginner who enjoys working with electronics, sensors, cameras, video, and software—and wants to use AI tools to turn ideas into working solutions.

## About the Role

You will help build solutions using ESP32 and similar hardware, sensors, cameras, and AI-powered software. Your projects will combine IoT, video processing, and AI vision with business applications and AIX’s AI-agent workflows.

This is a learning-oriented role. You do not need to be an expert in every area. We value practical projects, problem-solving, and the ability to learn quickly. You should be comfortable using AI coding tools while understanding, testing, and troubleshooting what you build.

## What You’ll Do

### Hardware and IoT

- Build and test prototypes using ESP32, ESP32-CAM, Arduino-compatible boards, Raspberry Pi, and similar hardware.

- Connect sensors for temperature, humidity, motion, distance, light, equipment status, and other business needs.

- Write and modify device software using Python, MicroPython, C/C++, or suitable tools.

- Connect devices to applications through Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, MQTT, and APIs.

- Assemble prototypes using breadboards, wiring, basic soldering, and enclosures.

### Cameras, Video, and AI Vision

- Set up cameras and capture images, video, and live streams.

- Help build AI-vision prototypes for tasks such as object detection, counting, presence detection, and visual inspection.

- Connect camera feeds to AI models or vision services running on suitable local hardware, servers, or cloud platforms.

- Combine camera observations with sensor readings to support business workflows.

- Test camera placement, lighting, image quality, detection accuracy, and response times.

- Help reduce false alerts and document situations where the system performs poorly.

- Follow project requirements for privacy, access control, and image or video retention.

### Software and AI Integration

- Use AI coding assistants to research components, write code, troubleshoot issues, and document solutions.

- Send sensor data and vision events to dashboards, databases, and business applications.

- Connect device and camera events to AIX’s AI Workers and AI Agents.

- Build alerts and approved automated actions based on sensor readings or visual events.

- Document wiring, components, code, setup instructions, and test results.

## Example Projects

| Business need | Example solution |

|---|---|

| Facility monitoring | Track temperature, humidity, and leaks, and send alerts when conditions require attention |

| Inventory visibility | Use cameras or sensors to detect item presence, count objects, or flag low stock |

| Visual inspection | Capture product images and help identify visible defects or missing components |

| Equipment monitoring | Combine sensor readings and camera observations to report equipment status |

| Operational monitoring | Detect activity or objects in defined areas and notify the appropriate team |

| AI-connected workflows | Have a sensor or vision event prompt an AIX AI Worker to log an issue, notify a team, or start an approved workflow |

## What We’re Looking For

- Basic hands-on experience with ESP32, Arduino, Raspberry Pi, or similar hardware.

- At least one project you can demonstrate or clearly explain.

- Basic programming ability in Python, MicroPython, or C/C++.

- Familiarity with basic electronics, sensors, wiring, and GPIO.

- Interest in cameras, video processing, computer vision, and AI.

- Comfort using AI tools while checking their output through testing.

- Patience with debugging hardware, software, and connectivity issues.

- Ability to document your work and explain what works, what does not, and what you would improve.

A degree is not required. Personal projects, maker experience, college projects, and self-directed learning are welcome. You do not need prior experience training AI models.

## Nice to Have — Not Required

- Experience with ESP32-CAM, USB cameras, Raspberry Pi cameras, or IP cameras.

- Exposure to OpenCV, object-detection models such as YOLO, or AI vision APIs.

- Familiarity with video streams and tools such as RTSP or FFmpeg.

- Experience with MQTT, REST APIs, JSON, or Node-RED.

- Basic Git and GitHub skills.

- Experience creating a simple dashboard or connecting a device to a database.

- Basic soldering, multimeter use, or enclosure assembly skills.

- Interest in edge AI and running models locally.

## What Success Looks Like in Your First 90 Days

With guidance from the team:

- Build a working sensor-based prototype connected to a software application.

- Set up a camera and demonstrate a simple AI-vision use case.

- Connect a sensor or vision event to an AIX AI-agent workflow.

- Test practical issues such as Wi-Fi interruptions, poor lighting, missed detections, and false alerts.

- Document the solution so another team member can reproduce it.

- Contribute to a pilot that addresses a clear business need.

## What You’ll Gain

- Hands-on experience across hardware, IoT, video, AI vision, and software.

- Opportunities to build solutions for real business use cases.

- Exposure to AIX’s agentic framework, AI Workers, and AI Agents.

- Experience taking an idea from an early prototype to a tested business pilot.

**Description**
Are you passionate about running large AI models directly on consumer devices — where every millisecond, milliwatt, and megabyte matters? Join our team to work at the core of the Neural Network Accelerator (NNA) software stack, driving on-device machine-learning inference, compiler and runtime development, and the automation infrastructure that ships production-quality AI features to millions of Amazon devices.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  
As a SysDE I on the NNA / EdgeAI team, you will contribute to the software stack that compiles, deploys, and runs vision and language models on Amazon's in-house neural accelerators. You will work across the ML compilation pipeline (quantization, graph lowering, kernel selection, artifact packaging), the on-device inference runtime (secure and non-secure execution paths, memory and bandwidth budgets), and the release and validation infrastructure that keeps our device fleet healthy build over build.

You will help build and improve the test and evaluation systems that validate model accuracy, latency, memory footprint, and stability on physical devices in the lab — including large-scale evaluation of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) end-to-end from reference to device. You will also contribute to the build, release, and CI automation that keeps our multi-package software stack shipping cleanly across product platforms.

* The Full Stack Developer – Corporate Risk Reporting role focuses on the risk visualization layer of the Corporate Risk Reporting (CRR) platform. * Within the CRR architecture, core risk logic is implemented in PostgreSQL, with curated risk results published into OpenSearch to support high-performance reporting, fuzzy filtering, and interactive exploration. **COLLABORATION:**

**CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT:**
Continuously evaluates and improves visualization patterns, technical approaches, and team practices to enhance the effectiveness and scalability of CRR risk reporting.

Minimum requirement of 3 years of relevant work experience, typically reflecting 5+ years in delivering full-stack applications in data-intensive or analytics-driven environments.

International Emerging Stores Payments (IESP) brings Amazon's payments products to customers in some of the fastest-growing markets in the world, across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), Asia Pacific (APAC) including India, and South America. These markets run on real-time payment rails such as UPI, on local wallets, cards, bill payments, and lending products, and on regulatory regimes that differ from one country to the next. Every one of those transactions depends on customer trust, and IESP Payments Security exists to earn and keep it.  
  
Payments Security owns full-stack Product Security for Payments across Amazon and its business units. We are part of Amazon's broader Stores Security organization, responsible for protecting Amazon's global information assets. We partner with Payments builder teams to make applications and infrastructure secure-by-design from concept to launch and into continuous operations, and we build the mechanisms, guardrails, and automation that let thousands of engineers do the right thing by default.  
  
As a software engineer on IESP Payments Security, you will build the software that makes security automatic for Amazon's payments businesses in MENA, APAC including India, and South America. Imagine writing the code that stops a vulnerability before it is merged, or an AI agent that scans hundreds of production applications and finds payment data stored where it should not be.  
  
You will work on three kinds of problems. First, controls-as-code: security rules and guardrails that run on every code change, including code written with AI assistance. Second, detection agents: AI-assisted services that find sensitive data, vulnerable patterns, and risky configurations across production. Third, onboarding acquired stacks: tooling that brings newly acquired businesses onto Amazon's standard engineering and security platforms. You will work side by side with security engineers, and your work will show up directly in fewer vulnerabilities and less time builders spend fixing them.  
You will own features and components end to end, from design through operation, and help mentor newer engineers.

You will spend most of your time building: designing services, writing and reviewing code, and shipping. You will pair with security engineers who bring a threat model or a class of findings, and together you will decide what can be automated and how to measure that it works.
